items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: And he played along in Silver Leaf Band with me. ... And we joined the Tuxedo Band and we got another bunch of fellows. ... Celestine, myself, Johnny Lindsay...

ctx.x: Do you remember about, excuse me, what year that was about? Was that...

That could have been about 1910. 1910, when you joined the Silver Leaf. Silver Leaf Band. I was still living in Jefferson Paris. And then I moved to New Orleans in 1911. And I was still with Silver Leaf Band. And Mr. Welch, he was a sickly man and he gave up the coinette playing. And we got over to the fellow by the name of Hippolyte Charles. He played coinette for us a while. And then he gave up the coinette playing and old man Welch came back again. And old man Welch made me to know Celestine. He said he was a…
You had already called it the Tuxedo Band though before you started the tuxedos. Is that right? Yes. And he was a big help to us.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Celestrian was one of the tronettes. When we first started playing, let me get that thing real. When we first started playing, we were with Henry Allen over the river, you see. We all used to play with him, you see.

ctx.x: Him and I played together, we is. Very nice color. And, uh, it's the attitude trombone, him and I. Peter Biker, Peter Biker, one of the tronettes. Celestrian was one of the tronettes. When we first started playing, let me get that thing real. When we first started playing, we were with Henry Allen over the river, you see. We all used to play with him, you see. And then we'd pull up and, you know, and I, and we'd take, I met in the other fellas to take the tuxedo bands, you see. I met in the other band. So, he was…

We used Adolph Alexander on the Alto. Was that the young Adolph Alexander or his father? No, no. The young Alexander played with me once, you know, in my history. Yes. He played, coming playing saxophone, Tornet, and playing saxophone.
